text:
Timo Meier went nine games without a goal while New Jersey won almost every night, then scored twice in the second period of Saturday's 4-0 win over Toronto. That's his season in miniature: the team is rolling, and he's been the guy doing everything but finishing.

He has three goals on 6.4 expected (the quality of his chances) and 70 shots, shooting 4.3% against a normal range of 8 to 12%. New Jersey has 59% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice and has still scored 5.2 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That's a lot of bad luck in one place, and it tends to even out.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.7 chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season (87th percentile), and Evolving-Hockey had his team creating noticeably more with him on the ice. The Devils visit Winnipeg next. Our projection sees about 24 goals, which means a lot more nights like Saturday.
